title: Best Single Trade
statement:
You get an array prices where prices[d] is the price of one share on day d.

You may make at most one trade: buy one share on one day and sell it on a later day. Return the largest profit you can make. If no trade makes money, return 0.

examples.why: Buy at 2, sell at 9. The lowest price 1 comes after the highest price 9, so max − min = 8 is not a real trade.
The price falls every day. Any trade loses money, so you do not trade.
Buy at 1, sell at 4. A new lowest price of 0 appears later, but it only leads to a profit of 2. Following the lowest price alone is not enough.

hints: Fix the selling day. Which buying day is best for it?
For a sale on day d, the best buy is the lowest price on any day before d. You can keep that number up to date as you walk forward.
One pass: track the lowest price so far and the best profit so far. At each day, first try selling at today's price against the lowest so far, then update the lowest.

explain.intuition:
Every trade is a pair (buy day, sell day) with buy before sell. Fix the sell day: the best buy for it is simply the cheapest day before it. So walk through the days once, remember the lowest price seen so far, and ask on each day: "if I sold today, what would I make?"

This is a window whose left edge jumps to a new low whenever one appears. The right edge is today. You never need to look back further, because an older, higher price can never be a better buy than the low you are holding.
steps: For each later price p: update best with p − lowest.
Then update lowest with p if it is lower.
Return best. It stays 0 when no day is above an earlier one.
pitfalls: Returning max(prices) − min(prices). The maximum can come before the minimum, as in [6, 2, 9, 1, 3].
Starting best at a negative number or returning a negative profit. Not trading is allowed, so the floor is 0.
Resetting best when a new low appears. The old best trade is still valid; a new low only matters for future sells.

solutions.title: Every buy and sell pair
solutions.idea: Try every buy day with every later sell day.

solutions.title: One pass with the lowest price so far
solutions.idea: For each day, the best trade that sells today buys at the cheapest earlier day. Track that minimum as you go.

followups: Return the buy and sell days as well. Which pair do you return if several trades tie?
You may now make as many trades as you like, holding at most one share at a time. What changes?
